title: The Fourth Runner
subtitle: 成功成就 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 成功成就（做人与做事·成功与成就）
meta: 主题语境：成功成就（做人与做事·成功与成就）　|　核心词汇：chance　|　正文 385 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 chance 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: I was the slowest boy in my year and nobody's idea of a champion. I had never won anything. So it was pure ① chance that I happened to be standing near the track when our teacher asked for a fourth runner for the relay. She looked at me, then at the empty lane, and said: '② Give him a chance.' That sentence changed my running, though it did not make me fast.

For three weeks I trained with the team. Any honest person could see there was little ③ chance that I would be picked for the final four: three boys were faster and one had won a medal last spring. Our coach never talked about prizes or medals, though chance, he often said, plays a smaller part than people imagine. 'Nobody ④ stands a chance of winning a race he has not run,' he said, and then he made me run it again and again.

In maths I was worse than in sport, but maths gave me one idea. I worked out how much time each boy lost in the bends, and mine was the worst by nearly a second and a half. ⑤ By chance I remembered something a sixth-form boy had told me: relays are won in the changeover, not in the straight. So I practised nothing but handing over the baton, three hundred times.

On the morning of the sports meet my legs felt heavy. 'Have you, ⑥ by any chance, practised handing over today?' our captain asked at the gate. I had not; I had practised for two weeks. In the third changeover our fastest boy slipped in the rain. I had ⑦ taken a chance on wearing my spikes, and I did not slip. I did not ⑧ chance a word about it to anybody until the following week.

We came third. Third is not a medal in our school, and the printed list only remembers the champion. But the sports master wrote in his report that our team had ⑨ taken a chance on a fifth-form nobody, and that it had paid off. Chance favours the prepared, people say; what nobody tells you is how long being prepared takes. Reading that report now, I think it was the real prize: somebody said ⑩ 'give him a chance' at exactly the moment when nobody else would have.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 可能性（there is (a) chance that ...）
C. n. 偶然；运气（by chance 偶然地）
D. v. 冒险；敢于做（chance sth）
E. 固定搭配：take a chance / take chances 冒险；碰运气
F. 固定搭配：by any chance 万一；或许（用于打听）
G. 固定搭配：stand a chance of 有……的希望／可能
H. 固定搭配：give sb a chance 给某人一个机会

items.q: it was pure chance that I happened to be standing
there was little chance that I would be picked
Nobody stands a chance of winning a race
Have you, by any chance, practised handing over
I had taken a chance on wearing my spikes
I did not chance a word about it
our team had taken a chance on a fifth-form nobody

answers.why: It was (pure) chance that ... 此处指“偶然得到的上场机会”，与下句老师替我争取的话直接呼应。
give sb a chance 是固定搭配，意为“给某人一个机会”，老师说这话时在替内向的我争取。
there is little chance that＋从句，意为“……的可能性极小”，指入选可能性。
stand a chance of＋动名词，意为“有……的希望”，教练用否定式鼓励人多跑。
by chance 意为“偶然地”，修饰 remembered，说明是无意想起。
by any chance 用于打听、语气委婉，意为“万一、不知道是不是”，队长的问话正合此境。
take a chance on＋动名词宾语，意为“冒险去做”，这里指冒险穿钉鞋。
chance a word 是动词用法，意为“敢开口说”，多用于否定，表示不敢提。
take a chance on sb 意为“在某人身上碰碰运气”，报告里说球队冒险启用了一个无名小卒。
与第 2 题形成首尾呼应，仍是 give sb a chance“给人机会”，此处强调时机之难得。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 我纯属偶然地站在跑道边。（by chance）
那位老师说：“给他一个机会。”（give sb a chance）
三周来，我入选最后四强的可能性很小。（there was little chance that）
没有跑过的比赛是不会有获胜希望的。（stand a chance of）
队长问我那天是否碰巧练过交接棒。（by any chance）
我们冒险让一名五年级的普通学生上场。（take a chance on）
answers: It was pure chance that I was standing by the track.
The teacher said, 'Give him a chance'.
For three weeks there was little chance that I would be picked for the final four.
Nobody stands a chance of winning a race he has not run.
The captain asked whether, by any chance, I had practised handing over the baton that day.
We took a chance on a fifth-form nobody.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 chance 的 3 种不同用法；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: By chance I was standing near the track when our teacher needed a fourth runner for the relay.
'Give him a chance,' she said, and that sentence changed the whole team.
There was little chance that I would be picked, since one boy had won a medal the spring before.
'Nobody stands a chance of winning a race he has not run,' my coach said, so I practised the changeover three hundred times.
I took a chance on wearing my spikes, and did not chance a word about it to the crowd afterwards.
We finished third, but the sports master later took a chance on me again, and that was the real prize.
